title: Savory Ricotta Béchamel
cScaleSummary: Approximately 12 mg cholesterol per serving, primarily from the part-skim ricotta, 2% milk, and Parmesan. The egg whites contain no cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: The recipe uses olive oil instead of butter and remains relatively low in cholesterol, but its dairy base, refined flour, and minimal fiber prevent it from being actively LDL-lowering.
intro: Béchamel began as a French white sauce and became deeply integrated into Italian cooking as besciamella, especially in the layered pastas of Emilia-Romagna. Italian-American lasagnas often pair ricotta with eggs instead, but this version joins the two traditions. A lightly infused olive-oil béchamel gives the filling savory depth, while part-skim ricotta adds body and two egg whites provide a gentle set. The result remains creamy enough to spread yet becomes stable and sliceable as the casserole bakes without becoming dense or rubbery.

stepGroups.title: Infuse the Milk
items: Combine {{ingredient:infusion-milk}} with {{ingredient:yellow-onion}}, {{ingredient:garlic}}, {{ingredient:bay-leaf}}, and {{ingredient:black-peppercorns}} in a saucepan.
Heat until steaming but not boiling. Remove from the heat, cover, and steep for 15 minutes.
Strain the infused milk and discard the aromatics. Measure the strained milk and add enough {{ingredient:reserved-milk}} to restore it to exactly {{quantity:infusion-milk}}.

stepGroups.title: Build the Béchamel
items: Heat {{ingredient:olive-oil}} in a clean saucepan over medium-low heat.
Whisk in {{ingredient:all-purpose-flour}} and cook for 2 to 3 minutes without allowing it to brown.
Gradually whisk in the warm infused milk. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, whisking frequently.
The béchamel is ready when it is completely smooth, heavily coats the back of a spoon, and briefly holds the tracks of the whisk.

stepGroups.title: Add the Ricotta
items: Remove the béchamel from the heat.
Process {{ingredient:part-skim-ricotta}} only until smooth, then whisk it and {{ingredient:parmesan}} into the warm béchamel until evenly incorporated.

stepGroups.title: Season and Cool
items: Season the ricotta béchamel with {{ingredient:kosher-salt}}, {{ingredient:nutmeg}}, and {{ingredient:ground-black-pepper}}.
Taste and correct the seasoning before adding the egg whites.
Let the mixture cool to 120°F to 130°F.

stepGroups.title: Incorporate the Egg Whites
items: Whisk {{ingredient:egg-whites}} in a small bowl just until loosened and fluid but not foamy.
Gently fold the egg whites into the ricotta béchamel until no visible streaks remain.
The finished mixture should be thick enough to spread without running while remaining creamy.

stepGroups.title: Hold the Ricotta Béchamel
items: Use the ricotta béchamel promptly, or cover and refrigerate it until ready to assemble the lasagna.
During baking, the roux and egg whites will give the layer a gentle, sliceable set without making it firm or rubbery.
